statement: Five general nonsingular plane conics have exactly 3264 nonsingular complex conics tangent to all five.

answer.qualification: Geometric conics for general inputs; the source recalls the complete-conic intersection calculation and cites its transversality justification. Double lines are extraneous.

source.location: Section “Chow Rings, Pentagons, and Real Conics”, printed pp. 5–6; unnumbered calculation C^5=3264 on p. 6
source.version: MPI MIS preprint 24/2019, containing arXiv:1902.05518v1; inspected calculation on printed p. 6

scope: Nonsingular plane conics tangent to five input plane conics; generic finite complex counts and real constructions have their own hypotheses.
notes:
Geometric conics for general inputs; the source recalls the complete-conic intersection calculation and cites its transversality justification. Double lines are extraneous.

The complex3264 count is classical Chasles; the modern paper’s certified all-real instance is a separate result.

Related literature. Détermination du nombre des sections coniques qui doivent toucher cinq courbes données d’ordre quelconque, ou satisfaire à diverses autres conditions (Michel Chasles, 1864). Historical or related contributions are retained here. Their own precise statements have not been independently verified for a separate result in this migration.

Source discussion. Five general nonsingular plane conics have exactly 3,264 nonsingular complex tangent conics. On the space of complete conics, C=2(P+L), and C^5=32(1+5·2+10·4+10·4+5·2+1)=3264. The calculation excludes the double-line component responsible for the naive 6^5 count.
